### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/environment-routing.mdx`  _(via HttpDispatcher (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via HttpDispatcher (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via HttpDispatcher (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via HttpDispatcher (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via HttpDispatcher (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **29** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1a6c330945dac00bb42fccd09f42e39ce510d8e1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2734aa658f9d6d331c2e6b436a65938997d8a9eb` — the merge of head `dd7562583d436be54100a980276c45e67e130510` into base `1a6c330945dac00bb42fccd09f42e39ce510d8e1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2734aa658f9d6d331c2e6b436a65938997d8a9eb && git checkout 2734aa658f9d6d331c2e6b436a65938997d8a9eb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1a6c330945dac00bb42fccd09f42e39ce510d8e1 dd7562583d436be54100a980276c45e67e130510 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1a6c330945dac00bb42fccd09f42e39ce510d8e1 && git merge --no-ff dd7562583d436be54100a980276c45e67e130510

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1a6c330945dac00bb42fccd09f42e39ce510d8e1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1a6c330945dac00bb42fccd09f42e39ce510d8e1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dd7562583d436be54100a980276c45e67e130510`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher-membership-revocation.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-list-projection-parity.test.ts + packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/authz-store-unavailable.ts, packages/runtime/src/api-endpoint-step.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.membership-skip-boundary.test.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts

Read: card #32230 (body and all 5 comments), PR #32919 (body, 2 comments, 5 files), the net diff against `main` (merge-base `474f7dbc`; `main` has not moved a scoped file since), and the 51 check-runs on this head: 35 `success`, 16 `skipped`, none failed, none pending.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set, at the environment-membership check (`judgeMembershipOf`, reached from `dispatch()` and from `environmentMembershipRefusal`):

1. A principal with no `sys_environment_member` row for the resolved environment is answered `403 PROJECT_MEMBERSHIP_REQUIRED` on every request, the first one after the row is removed included. On `main` a positive verdict stood for its 60 s TTL, per dispatcher instance. Narrowing. **Right**: it is the card's Expected and ruling A.
2. A principal whose membership read cannot be made, or throws, is answered the outage (`AuthzStoreUnavailableError`, 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`) on every request; a verdict from an earlier request no longer stands in for the read. Narrowing. **Right**: it carries the fail-closed read of #21941 to every caller, and the claim comment records the ruling as accepting it.
3. Nothing widens. The removed field held positive verdicts only, so no path that answered 403 or threw now answers `null`. A member who is added is admitted on the next request, as before.
4. Unchanged: enforcement off, no resolved environment, the system environment, the platform organization, the path skips of `enforceProjectMembership`, a composition that registers no member object, and the no-principal fallback.
5. Role change, which the card's Expected also names: the check reads row presence only. The dispatcher is the only non-test reader of the member object in this tree and it does not read `role`, so no role verdict exists here to go stale.
6. Cost: one `find` (`limit: 1`) per gated request for a member, where it was at most one per TTL per instance. The claim comment records the ruling as accepting it.

Public surface: none moves. No export, option, config key, wire shape or error code is added or removed; both answers above already exist. Two `private` members leave the `HttpDispatcher` class, and no other file in the tree names them.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/runtime`, the one package whose published source moves: **right**. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right (nothing a metadata author writes changes), and AGENTS.md step 3 ships a non-protocol breaking change as `patch` with its BREAKING banner and its ADR-0087 disposition. Both are in the changeset (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: nothing authorable is removed, so no FROM/TO mapping is owed).
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: **right**, line-initial on the PR body and on the changeset body. Judgments 1 to 3: a narrowing, no widening, no public surface.
- `Skills-docs: none`: holds. No file under `skills/` names the check, its error code or the member object, and no page under `content/docs` or `docs/` states a reuse window.
- `Check Changeset` and the lint gates are green on this head.
- nit (prose face, for the seat's sentence check): "reads the membership store for every scoped request" and "once per scoped request" are wider than the code. The platform-organization bypass and the path skips of `enforceProjectMembership` answer before the read.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Ruling A, escalated to the lane seat.** The card carries the ruling as the seat's relay (claim comments 6838259317 and 6838313925), not in the maintainer's own words, and the card body proposed invalidation instead. The diff implements the ruling as relayed and as this review's brief names it. The seat confirms the verbatim ruling is on record before landing.
- **Dogfood battery, escalated to the lane seat.** A `!` / `(narrowing)` PR owes a dogfood battery pinned to its head. The PR body says its readings "go to the card's seat report and into this body when they land"; neither carries them. On this head the dogfood shard matrix and `Dogfood Verify CLI` concluded `skipped`, and the aggregate `Dogfood Regression Gate` is `success`. This is the seat's pre-queue check, not a contract finding.
- The PR body names its head as `b7b373fd` and describes the parity suite as changed by "one comment". The reviewed head is one commit later and also adds a side-effect import to that file; ④ judges it. nit, PR body only.
- The two gates the dev could not complete locally (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`): answered by the head's check-runs, all green or skipped.
- The ablation the body reports (4 of 7 red) was not re-run. Read statically it agrees: cases 1 to 4 each need a second read to see the store change, and cases 5 to 7 pass either way.
- The card's cross-replica invalidation channel is moot: no per-instance state is left to invalidate.
- No `open_questions` entry is in the input set. The PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no author note is owed.

### ④ Design judgment

Against the published spec on `main`: `api.enforceProjectMembership` is declared as the per-environment membership 403 gate, and the dispatcher plugin's option says it returns 403 for non-members. Neither declares a reuse window. The narrowing takes no declared capability away; it makes the declared refusal hold from the first request after a removal.

- `packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts` — **holds.** The field, its TTL constant, the read, the write and the expiry delete are all gone. `judgeMembershipOf` reaches the registry probe and `ql.find` on every call, and both doors end in it. The class keeps no other verdict between requests (its two remaining memos are the `/ready` probes), and the engine keeps no find-result cache. Each comment sentence agrees with the code: the outage arms are the two `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` throws below the comment, and the cited rule is stated in `resolve-authz-context.ts` in those terms (a success is cached only where the engine exposes the write epoch and the middleware seam; the TTL is the residual bound). The rule reaches as far as the engine's read: the dispatcher adds no staleness of its own.
  - nit: the JSDoc block that now carries the rule sentence is detached from `enforceProjectMembership`; a second JSDoc block follows it, above `enforceAuthGate`. It is detached on `main` already.
- `packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher-membership-revocation.test.ts` — **holds.** Cases 1 to 4 fail under any reuse of a verdict. The 503 case pins the brand, the code, the status and `object: 'sys_environment_member'`, so no other read's outage can satisfy it. Two dispatchers over one store stand for two replicas.
  - nit: "admitted" is asserted as the absence of the membership 403, not as a served answer. The endpoint-door case pins the 403 arm only; the outage arm on that door rests on the shared function.
- `packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.test.ts` — **holds.** The fixture hands back `opts.memberRows` by reference on each read, so the second call sees the truncation. The retired call-count assertion pinned the reuse itself.
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-list-projection-parity.test.ts` — **holds.** The rewritten sentence is true of the dispatcher at this head. The side-effect import is the package's established collection-time pattern and moves no assertion.
- Cited, outside the diff: `packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.membership-skip-boundary.test.ts:35` still lists "a cached membership" among the ways the check answers `null`. nit, comment only: a follow-up card or a prose-only edit.

Findings: 0 must-fix, 0 should-fix, 5 nits. Nits alone end the round.
